verdict: OPEN (new entrants still getting distribution) — verified post-mid-2024 launches (DisastersUncovered, Forgotten Disasters, Disasters At Sea) are receiving real algorithmic distribution into July 2026, but the niche is narrowing: median outcomes below the breakouts are low-four-figure views, the 2025-26 AI-content crackdown adds monetization risk, and my discovery method structurally under-counts dead channels, so the true failure base rate is higher than the visible cohort suggests.

evidence_summary:
METHOD: Discovery via WebSearch (youtube.com HTML and most stats directories — similarchannels, favoree, playboard, graphtreon, patreon, feedspot, findachannel — were 403-blocked at the egress proxy; search.list quota exhausted per instructions), then every number verified via YouTube Data API v3 channels.list / playlistItems.list / videos.list on 2026-07-12. Census also mined curated public playlists via playlistItems.list to enumerate small channels.

COHORT FINDINGS (created since mid-2024, exact format = faceless calm-narration disaster docs): only TWO genuinely indie entrants with traction were findable — DisastersUncovered (2024-12, 26.6k subs, 3.76M views; last-30-day uploads repeatedly >100k views on a 26.6k-sub channel = live algorithmic distribution) and Forgotten Disasters (2025-09, 7.1k subs, 837k views in 10 months, median upload ~4.2k). Two licensed-TV channels of the same vintage (Disasters At Sea 72.6k/10.5M; DisasterTV 13.8k but recent uploads 25-1,300 views) prove demand but not the indie playbook. Verified failures: The Disaster Diaries (Apr 2024, 1 video, 172 views), Disaster Digest (Nov 2023, 1.04M lifetime views collapsed to 62-820 views/upload), two 'Disaster Documentaries' channels squatting the keyword for years at 234/835 subs, plus a renamed-and-emptied 'Disaster Files'. CRITICAL CAVEAT: absence of visible H1-2026 zero-traction launches is a defect of my discovery method, not evidence they don't exist — search engines only index channels that already got views, so the failure denominator is systematically undercounted and the visible cohort overstates success odds.

LONG-TAIL DEMAND (Q2): at marquee tier demand is geography-independent — Fascinating Horror non-Anglosphere videos sampled: Gansu Ultramarathon (China) 1,095,650; Ponte Morandi (Italy) 664,056; Salang Pass (Afghanistan) 656,525; Ycuá Bolaños fire (Paraguay) 531,803; Formosa Fun Coast (Taiwan) 440,348; Loveparade (Germany) 410,491; Iraq poison-grain 392,443; Katerina Didenko (Russia) 370,986; Ajka toxic sludge (Hungary) 313,846; Sewol (Korea) 313,254; Filair Let-410 (DR Congo) 238,540. Below marquee tier the same long-tail topics pull 1-3 orders of magnitude less: DisastersUncovered — Tuvalu dormitory fire 7,114; Angers Bridge (France) 14,399; Iolaire 8,216; Cavalese-1998 49,120 (but Cavalese-1976 broke out at 291,912); Forgotten Disasters — Mount Pelée (Martinique) 2,213; Glen Cinema 4,029; Moorgate 1,657. Demand below the marquee tier is real but authority-gated: topic selection alone does not transfer FH-scale views.

MONETIZATION (Q3): Fascinating Horror links Patreon in 100/100 sampled descriptions (patron count unretrievable — Patreon/Graphtreon blocked; page shows 460 patron-only posts); sponsor reads are sparse at marquee tier (Factor in ~3 of 100 FH videos; no VPN/audiobook reads observed). Sponsors DO buy reads far down-market: Forgotten Disasters (7k subs) carries Aura and Factor. Policy risk is elevated: YouTube's Jul-2025 'inauthentic content' YPP overhaul and the early-2026 AI-slop demonetization wave (channel-level enforcement; faceless human creators reported as collateral damage — TheNextWeb, Hollywood Reporter) is reshaping the niche; DisastersUncovered now titles every video 'No AI / Human Narrated' — direct market evidence of both AI-channel flooding and demonetization fear. YouTube's advertiser-friendly guidelines classify 'sensitive events'/tragedy as limited-ads territory; tragedy channels mitigate via no-graphic-imagery house style (FH's stated approach) plus Patreon.

answers.question: (1) Enumerate all disaster-documentary channels created since mid-2024 and their trajectories — is DisastersUncovered repeatable or a lottery ticket?
answers.answer: Verified census of post-mid-2024 launches in/near the exact format: DisastersUncovered (2024-12; 26.6k subs, 3.76M views, 63 videos — thriving, recent uploads 2.3k-292k views with 6 of last 20 over 100k); Forgotten Disasters (2025-09; 7.1k subs, 837k views, 59 videos — modest, median ~4.2k/upload); Disasters At Sea (2025-05; 72.6k subs, 10.5M views — thriving but licensed Blue Ant TV content); DisasterTV (2025-09; 13.8k subs but recent uploads 25-1,300 views — licensed TV, currently failing); The Disaster Diaries (2024-04; 2 subs, 1 video — dead). Near-cohort: Disaster Digest (2023-11) got ~1M views then collapsed to 62-820 views/upload — traction in this niche can be revoked. Verdict on repeatability: DisastersUncovered is PARTIALLY repeatable — Forgotten Disasters proves a Sept-2025 entrant still gets distribution and sponsors, and DisastersUncovered's own July-2026 uploads still outperform its sub count — but it is the ONLY indie breakout of its vintage I could find, my method cannot see zero-view launches (survivorship bias in discovery, stated explicitly), and Disaster Digest shows the downside path. Treat it as: distribution door open, median outcome ~1-5k views/video after a year of grinding, breakout probability real but low.

answers.question: (2) Does demand hold below the marquee tier — view counts on genuinely long-tail/non-Anglosphere disaster videos (10-15 sampled)?
answers.answer: Sampled 15+ long-tail/non-Anglosphere videos (all API-verified 2026-07-12). Marquee tier (Fascinating Horror, 1.44M subs): geography is no penalty — Gansu Ultramarathon (China) 1,095,650; Ponte Morandi (Italy) 664,056; Salang Pass (Afghanistan) 656,525; Ycuá Bolaños (Paraguay) 531,803; Formosa Fun Coast (Taiwan) 440,348; Loveparade (Germany) 410,491; Iraq poison grain 392,443; Didenko (Russia) 370,986; Ajka sludge (Hungary) 313,846; Sewol (S. Korea) 313,254; Filair crash (DR Congo) 238,540; BOAC 911 (Japan) 275,995 — every FH main upload clears ~170k regardless of obscurity. Sub-marquee tier: same class of topics pulls 1-2 orders of magnitude less — DisastersUncovered (26.6k subs): Tuvalu dormitory fire 7,114; Angers Bridge (France, 1850) 14,399; Iolaire 8,216; Cavalese-1998 49,120 vs Cavalese-1976 breakout 291,912; Forgotten Disasters (7k subs): Mount Pelée (Martinique, 30,000 dead) 2,213; Glen Cinema 4,029; Moorgate 1,657; Matawan 752. Conclusion: demand below the marquee is real but channel-authority-gated — obscure non-Anglosphere topics reliably monetize attention only once the channel itself has distribution; the topic catalog is not a moat, and saturated 'famous' topics (Boston Molasses: 2,293 views on DisastersUncovered) can underperform obscure ones.

answers.question: (3) Monetization on tragedy content — limited ads, Fascinating Horror's Patreon scale, sponsor presence?
answers.answer: Three verified signals plus one gap. (a) Patreon: Fascinating Horror links Patreon in 100/100 of its last 100 video descriptions and the page shows 460 patron-gated posts — it is a load-bearing revenue leg — but exact patron/income figures were unretrievable (Patreon and Graphtreon both 403-blocked at my egress proxy); treat scale as unverified. (b) Sponsors: sparse at marquee tier — Factor reads in only ~3 of FH's last 100 videos, and no VPN/audiobook reads observed in that sample; but sponsors do buy tragedy-adjacent inventory far down-market: Forgotten Disasters carries Aura and Factor reads at just 7k subs, and DisastersUncovered ran Factor at ~26k subs. (c) Ad policy risk: YouTube's advertiser-friendly guidelines put 'sensitive events'/tragedy in limited-ads territory, which is precisely why the FH house style (no graphic imagery, respectful tone) exists; more materially, the July-2025 YPP 'inauthentic content' overhaul and the early-2026 mass demonetization of AI/faceless channels (channel-level enforcement, human faceless creators hit as collateral damage per Hollywood Reporter/TheNextWeb) is the dominant 2026 monetization risk — DisastersUncovered now stamps 'No AI. Human Narrated.' into every title as a survival signal. Gap: no first-person RPM/limited-ads report from FH or peers surfaced in indexed sources; that number remains unverified.
